items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-11-10
items.q: Robert Morton and Ray McNamara were the organist. And I used to stay down there at night to close...

ctx.x: I've heard him on records, huh?

Witt Lebowski. He had a brother who was a violinist. But Witt Lebowski had a way that he could break a string on a piano. Very easily. If he was mad at you, he'd close the piano down and put his feet up on the piano like this and wouldn't touch it. They had Tony Papalia was with him down there. Jimmy Boyle. Johnny Karugi was on fiddle. And the funny thing about it, Robert Morton and Ray McNamara were the organist. And I used to stay down there at night to close, to put, I don't know if I told you, to put the trap…

items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-10-27
items.q: That's where I got to know Ray McNamara and Bob Martin on the organ... And that's how I got to know Bob Martin and Ray McNamara.

ctx.x: Well, did they have any fakers out there? No?

No, they were all readers. They played overtures and things like that. Overtures and played, that's how I got to know all this crap. I mean, in fact, when I went to this, when I was in high school, I got a job at the Liberty Theater as an usher working just weekends in high school during the school season. I think we got a dollar or two dollars a day. And you'd always get tips on Saturday and Sunday when you'd have an over crowd of people and you'd get people to sit. You have one of these flash boxes with green…
That's a trick. They don't know that you made a mistake.
